IB A3 Databases

SQL Worksheets

Work in sequence. The first worksheet is only about reading a schema and writing clean SELECT queries. The second moves on to sorting, pattern matching, joins, and a first grouped report. The third opens a blank workspace so students build the database themselves with DDL and DML. Higher Level students then continue with aggregate functions: COUNT, AVG, SUM, MAX, MIN, GROUP BY, and HAVING.

Basic retrieval first Sorting and joins next Build from scratch last HL aggregates
Open SQL Playground Back to A3

How to Use the Sequence

  • Keep the worksheet in one tab and the playground in another.
  • Do not jump ahead: each dataset assumes the previous one is already secure.
  • The final SL worksheet opens a blank workspace because students are building the schema themselves.

SL Coverage

  • A3.1 relational features, keys, integrity, benefits, and limitations
  • A3.2 schema reading, ERDs, data types, table structure, normal forms, and 3NF thinking
  • A3.3 SELECT, filtering, ordering, joins, plus CREATE, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE

Worksheet 1 | Core Retrieval

School Library

Start here. Use one clean three-table database to learn the structure of a relational model, then practise SELECT, FROM, WHERE, AND, and OR without extra SQL features getting in the way.

Worksheet 2 | Next-Step Queries

Campus Clubs

Move here once basic filtering is secure. This worksheet assumes students already know retrieval basics and focuses on ORDER BY, DISTINCT, LIKE, BETWEEN, joins, and a first GROUP BY report.

A3.2.2 A3.2.4 A3.3.2

Worksheet 3 | Build the Database

Canteen Orders

Finish the SL sequence by building the database yourself in a blank workspace. Students work from the schema and ERD, create the tables, insert starter rows in batches, and then apply UPDATE and DELETE.

Worksheet 4 | HL Focus

Course Enrolment Reporting

Use a ready-made HL dataset to practise grouped counts, averages, totals, highest and lowest values, and grouped filtering with HAVING.

COUNT AVG SUM MAX / MIN HAVING

Worksheet 5 | HL Synthesis

Build the House Competition Database

Optional extension. Start from a blank workspace, build the schema from the ERD, batch-load a small starter dataset, and then answer aggregate-report questions.

Teacher Flow

Use the worksheet order to control the scaffolding. The playground stays the same; the worksheet is what narrows the focus.

After SL Core

Once the first three worksheets are secure, Higher Level students move to Course Enrolment for grouped calculations, views, and transactions.
